canvas-01-1.description: Part 1 of the map on printed sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the centre of Haworth east of the West Shore Railroad, from the borough line at the top to St. Nicholas Avenue at the bottom and from Summit Avenue beside the tracks to Hill Street. The railroad, lettered W. S. R. R., and a parallel street marked not named cross the upper left. Above the Haworth Drive boulevard, Nevada Place, Stevens Street and Harland Avenue frame the large open blocks 120 and 121 with a stone dwelling, the narrow lots of blocks 122, 126 and 127, block 123, and block 128 with the Haworth Public School and its play grounds, east of Valley Road (lettered Owasco St. or Valley Road). South of the boulevard the blocks between Terrace, Stevens Place, Owatonna Street and Valley Road are divided into narrow numbered lots; they hold the civic centre of the town: the fire department and borough hall and the post office on Terrace, the Congregational church and the Community House near Owatonna Street, and a gasoline station by Park Street. Blocks 130 and 136 between the tracks and Terrace belong to sheet 4. Dwellings are few and mostly frame. Six-inch water pipes run in Haworth Drive, Terrace, Owatonna Street and Valley Road. The upper half of the page, with the title, key, notes, specials index and a key map of the borough at 1000 feet to an inch, is not part of this map.
notes: Printed sheet 1 (canvas 1); the key map in the upper half is at 1000 ft to an inch and is not georeferenced.
Placed only by the Haworth Drive row (Terrace Street, Owatonna Street, Valley Road), hand-picked at the centre of the drawn boulevard: a helmert transformation, low confidence away from that row.

St. Nicholas Avenue east of the railroad is drawn about 180 m south of Haworth Drive; today's street is about 25 m closer, so its junctions were not used. Nevada Place and Harland Avenue east of Park Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
Stevens Place is drawn straight; today's Stevens Place curves and was left out.
Haworth Public School, fire department and borough hall, post office, Congregational church and Community House are on this part.

Printed sheet 1. Upper half: title, legend, water and fire notes, specials index and a key map of the borough at 1000 ft to an inch (not georeferenced). Lower half at 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line along Park Street: part 1 east of the West Shore Railroad (Summit Av [now Houston Place] to Hill St, Harland Av to St. Nicholas Av: Terrace, Stevens St and Stevens Pl, Nevada Pl, Owatonna, Owasco St or Valley Rd, Haworth Drive boulevard [Haworth Avenue], borough hall, public school); part 2 west of the railroad (Maple St to Park St, Elm Av to Haworth Drive; blocks 78, 81, 85). Part 1 has street control only on the Haworth Drive row (helmert); St. Nicholas Av east of the railroad is drawn about 25 m south of today's street.

canvas-01-2.description: Part 2 of the map on printed sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the blocks of Haworth just west of the West Shore Railroad: from Maple Street on the west to Park Street on the east, and from the borough line north of Elm Avenue down across Orchard Avenue and Harland Avenue to the Haworth Drive boulevard. It shows block 74 along the top, block 78 between Elm and Orchard Avenues, block 81 between Orchard and Harland Avenues and block 85 between Harland Avenue and Haworth Drive, each divided into large numbered lots. Building is sparse: a handful of one- and two-storey frame dwellings, two of concrete block, garages and a small store along Harland Avenue, and a note at the left edge pointing to a concrete-block dwelling 230 feet to the west in block 77. A stream crosses the upper left of block 78, and a north arrow is drawn inside it. A six-inch water pipe runs in Maple Street, Harland Avenue and Haworth Drive. Park Street, at the right edge, is cut by the heavy line dividing this part from part 1.
notes: Printed sheet 1 (canvas 1), lower left.
Orchard Avenue is Orchard Place in OpenStreetMap; Haworth Drive (Haworth Avenue) is Haworth Avenue.

Park Street is cut by the part line; its junctions were hand-picked as the drawn west edge plus 30 ft. The Elm Avenue and Orchard Avenue junctions with Park Street disagreed with the fit by 7 to 9 m (Park Street has been realigned near Elm Avenue) and were not used.
Placed by 5 control points (2 detected on Maple Street, 3 hand-picked): medium to low confidence.

Printed sheet 1. Upper half: title, legend, water and fire notes, specials index and a key map of the borough at 1000 ft to an inch (not georeferenced). Lower half at 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line along Park Street: part 1 east of the West Shore Railroad (Summit Av [now Houston Place] to Hill St, Harland Av to St. Nicholas Av: Terrace, Stevens St and Stevens Pl, Nevada Pl, Owatonna, Owasco St or Valley Rd, Haworth Drive boulevard [Haworth Avenue], borough hall, public school); part 2 west of the railroad (Maple St to Park St, Elm Av to Haworth Drive; blocks 78, 81, 85). Part 1 has street control only on the Haworth Drive row (helmert); St. Nicholas Av east of the railroad is drawn about 25 m south of today's street.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the eastern half of Haworth between Haworth Drive and Madison Avenue at the top and Massachusetts Avenue, the Dumont boundary, at the bottom, and from Hill Street on the west to Garfield Street on the east. Schraalenburgh Road runs down the sheet a third of the way across; west of it lie the large lots of block 135, with the Episcopal church and a gasoline station facing Haworth Drive, and the open ground of Section 10 with a few dwellings, while Hill Street and Summit Place in the lower left are lined with narrow numbered lots and small frame dwellings. East of the road, blocks 181 to 183B (Section 13) are mostly open, with a few dwellings and outbuildings. The rest of the sheet is a regular grid of long blocks divided into narrow lots: Pine, Chestnut, Beacon, Pleasant, Whitman and Garfield Streets run north and south between Madison Avenue, Hardenburgh Avenue and Massachusetts Avenue, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a few of concrete block, and many unbuilt lots. A strip of blocks 170 to 175 north of Madison Avenue is drawn along the top edge; block 170 holds the fire department house on Schraalenburgh Road. An abandoned water tank stands in the median of Haworth Drive, an automobile repair shop at Schraalenburgh Road and Massachusetts Avenue, and water pipes of six and eight inches run in most streets. The borough line along Massachusetts Avenue is marked, and the ground beyond it, with Washington Avenue, is left to the map of Dumont. The compass rose is on the left; the title cartouche and scale are at the top right and bottom right.
notes: Haworth Drive (lettered with "Haworth Av." in its median) is Haworth Avenue in OpenStreetMap; it is drawn as a 120-foot boulevard.
Haworth Drive, Madison Avenue and Schraalenburgh Road meet offset; that junction was left out of the control.
Hill Street ends today short of Haworth Avenue; only its junction with Massachusetts Avenue survives, and it was not detected.
Fire department house at 1130 Madison Avenue end of block 170; Episcopal church in block 135; an abandoned 40-foot water tank in the Haworth Drive median.
The Massachusetts Avenue junctions along the Dumont line were not detected; the sheet is controlled by the Madison and Hardenburgh Avenue rows.

100 ft. One part. East side: Haworth Drive and Madison Av to Massachusetts Av (Dumont line), Hill St and Summit Pl to Garfield St: Schraalenburgh Rd, Pine, Chestnut, Beacon, Pleasant, Whitman, Hardenburgh Av; blocks 135-197. Massachusetts Av row not detected; Haworth Av/Madison/Schraalenburgh junction excluded (offset streets).

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the western part of Haworth, from Haworth Avenue and the Haworth Drive boulevard at the top to New Avenue, unopened, on the Delford and Dumont lines at the bottom, and from Westview Terrace to Brook Street. Along the top edge a strip of blocks 43, 44 and 82 lines the north side of Haworth Avenue between Chestnut, Balder and Mill Streets. Below it the open ground of Section 3 and the White Beeches Golf and Country Club, whose club house stands in the golf links of block 48, take up the centre of the sheet; Haworth Drive winds south through them from Haworth Avenue to Sunset Avenue, becoming S. Haworth Drive. East of Haworth Drive, around St. Nicholas Avenue, Beech Street (Norwood Avenue) and The Crescent, the blocks 86 to 96 are laid out in large lots with scattered frame and concrete-block dwellings; Lakeside West and Lakeside East follow a brook that runs south through the sheet past the golf links to a pond in block 106. The lower strip, along Haworth Drive (the west end of today's Sunset Avenue), Sunset Avenue and Sylvan Avenue, crossed by Westview Terrace, St. Albans Place, S. Haworth Drive and Eastview Terrace, is subdivided into house lots with many one- and two-storey dwellings. A narrow strip of Section 4 along the west edge is marked no exposure. The upper left of the sheet is taken up by an inset (part 2) bounded by a heavy line. The compass rose is at the upper left and the scale at the lower right.
notes: Mill Street is now the north end of Haworth Drive; St. Nicholas Avenue west of Haworth Drive is Mc Culloch Place in OpenStreetMap.
The east-west street lettered Haworth Drive at the lower left is the west end of today's Sunset Avenue; Sylvan Avenue here is Sylvan Place West.
Haworth Drive (Haworth Avenue) east of Mill Street is a 120-foot boulevard; its junctions with Lakeside East and Brook Street were left out because they are measured on one roadway.
White Beeches Golf and Country Club house (heated by steam, electric light) in block 48.
New Avenue is marked not opened; the ground beyond the borough line is left to the map of Dumont.
Brook Street is cut by the east edge of the sheet.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Haworth Av and Haworth Drive boulevard to New Av, Westview Ter to Brook St: Chestnut, Balder, Mill (now Haworth Drive north of Haworth Av), St. Nicholas Av (west part now Mc Culloch Place), Beech (Norwood Av), Lakeside West and East, The Crescent, Ivy, Haworth Drive and S. Haworth Drive, Sunset Av, Haworth Drive west of S. Haworth Drive (now Sunset Avenue), Sylvan Av (now Sylvan Place West), St. Albans Pl, Eastview Ter; White Beeches Golf and Country Club. Part 2 (inset, upper left, 100 ft): Garfield, Grant, Harrison and Franklin Sts between Madison and Hardenburgh Avs and south of Hardenburgh, the Demarest line (The Antlers hotel).

sheet-3-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 3 is an inset at the upper left of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and bounded by a heavy line, showing the easternmost blocks of Haworth beyond sheet 2: Garfield, Grant, Harrison and Franklin Streets between Madison Avenue and Hardenburgh Avenue, with the north ends of the blocks south of Hardenburgh Avenue. Blocks 176 to 179 north of Madison Avenue appear along the top, blocks 188 to 191 fill the middle, and blocks 198 to 201 the bottom. Every block is divided into narrow numbered house lots facing the north-south streets, with lot numbers along both sides. Building is sparse: a dozen one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a concrete-block dwelling on Madison Avenue at Garfield Street, a few garages, and The Antlers, a two-and-a-half-storey frame hotel, on Hardenburgh Avenue between Harrison and Franklin Streets. The Borough of Haworth line with the Borough of Demarest runs down the east side of the inset just beyond Franklin Street; the area outside the inset is marked no exposure. Six-inch water pipes run in Madison and Hardenburgh Avenues and in Garfield, Grant and Harrison Streets.
notes: The Antlers hotel on Hardenburgh Avenue, listed in the specials index on sheet 1.
The inset continues sheet 2 eastward to the Demarest line; Garfield Street is the boundary street shared with sheet 2.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Haworth Av and Haworth Drive boulevard to New Av, Westview Ter to Brook St: Chestnut, Balder, Mill (now Haworth Drive north of Haworth Av), St. Nicholas Av (west part now Mc Culloch Place), Beech (Norwood Av), Lakeside West and East, The Crescent, Ivy, Haworth Drive and S. Haworth Drive, Sunset Av, Haworth Drive west of S. Haworth Drive (now Sunset Avenue), Sylvan Av (now Sylvan Place West), St. Albans Pl, Eastview Ter; White Beeches Golf and Country Club. Part 2 (inset, upper left, 100 ft): Garfield, Grant, Harrison and Franklin Sts between Madison and Hardenburgh Avs and south of Hardenburgh, the Demarest line (The Antlers hotel).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the centre-west of Haworth from the Haworth Drive boulevard at the top to New Avenue, unopened, on the Dumont line at the bottom, and from Brook Street on the west to the West Shore Railroad and Summit Avenue on the east. The upper half is a regular grid of large blocks (89 to 99) between Brook, Myrtle and Maple Streets and Park Street, which runs diagonally beside the railroad, crossed by St. Nicholas Avenue and Beech Street (lettered Norwood Avenue), with Ivy Avenue, marked not opened west of Maple Street. Most lots are vacant; a few frame dwellings and garages stand on them, and the Sacred Heart Roman Catholic church faces Beech Street near Park Street. South of Ivy Avenue the golf links of block 100 fill the west side, with a pond edge at the lower left, while blocks 101 to 111 between Myrtle Street, Maple Street and Park Street, along Jefferson, Sunset and Sylvan Avenues, are more closely built with one- and two-storey frame, concrete-block and brick-veneer dwellings. Islington Place runs diagonally from Sunset Avenue to New Avenue in the lower left. The railroad, lettered W. S. R. R., crosses the sheet as a band of tracks with a wood bridge at Ivy Avenue; the passenger and freight depots stand east of it at the top right, and blocks 130 and 136 along Summit Avenue and St. Nicholas Avenue, east of the tracks, are drawn in part. Section 9 east of the railroad is blank. Water pipes of six inches run in most streets; a compass rose and the scale are on the sheet.
notes: Islington Place is Paulson Place in OpenStreetMap; Sylvan Avenue east of Islington Place is Sylvan Place East; Beech Street is lettered with the alternative name Norwood Avenue.

Summit Avenue, east of the railroad, is Houston Place in OpenStreetMap; Houston Place / St. Nicholas Avenue was rejected (about 15 m), so St. Nicholas Avenue east of the tracks no longer follows its 1924 line.

Haworth Drive (Haworth Avenue) is a 120-foot boulevard; its junctions with Brook, Myrtle and Maple Streets were hand-picked at the centre of the drawn boulevard, since the detector measured them on one roadway.
West Shore Railroad passenger depot and freight house at the top right; Sacred Heart R.C. Church on Beech Street; wood bridge carrying Ivy Avenue over the railroad.
Ivy Avenue west of Maple Street and New Avenue are marked not opened.

100 ft. One part. Haworth Drive boulevard to New Av, Brook St to Summit Av east of the West Shore Railroad: Myrtle, Maple, Park, Islington Pl (now Paulson Place), St. Nicholas Av, Beech (Norwood Av), Ivy, Jefferson, Sunset, Sylvan Av (now Sylvan Place East); passenger and freight depots, Sacred Heart R.C. Church. Haworth Avenue boulevard junctions hand-picked at the drawn boulevard centre (the detector measured them on one roadway). East of the railroad the part disagrees with canvas-01-1 by about 10 to 17 m (extrapolated beyond its control; Houston Place / St. Nicholas Avenue rejected).
